# 1 Maccabees Chapter 16 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 16 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 16 is the final chapter of 1 Maccabees. It ends on a note of brutal treachery — Simon's assassination by his son-in-law Ptolemy — and closes with the "rest of the acts" formula that mirrors the ending formulas of the books of Kings (cf. 2 Kgs 8:23, etc.). This deliberate literary ending signals the book's conscious modeling on the Deuteronomistic History. The abruptness is intentional: John Hyrcanus survived and became a long-reigning high priest, but the author ends here, at the threshold.

**Key term rulings:**
- "by his mercy" / "by God's mercy" (v.3) — EMET "by his mercy" (referring to God); SOPHIA: "by God's mercy" to clarify the antecedent
- "help from Heaven" (v.3) — preserved; consistent with the book's avoidance of "God" in direct narrative (God acts but is rarely named directly in 1 Maccabees)
- "a great act of treachery" (v.17) — retained; the author's moral summary
- "the annals of his high priesthood" (v.24) — deliberate echo of the Kings formula; preserved exactly
- The Shebat dating (v.14) — Hebrew month name preserved; the only Hebrew month name used in the book
- The assassination scene (vv.15-16): rendered without softening; the horror is part of the narrative

---

**1** John came up from Gazara and reported to his father Simon what Cendebaeus had done.

**2** Simon summoned his two elder sons Judas and John and said to them: "My brothers and I and my father's house have fought the wars of Israel from our youth until this day, and it has been given to us to deliver Israel many times.

**3** But now I am old, and you, by God's mercy, are of mature age. Take my place and my brother's place and go out and fight for our nation; and may help from Heaven be with you."

**4** He mustered from the country twenty thousand men of war and cavalry, and they marched against Cendebaeus and spent the night at Modein.

**5** They arose in the morning and marched into the plain, and behold, a great army met them — infantry and cavalry — and between them was a stream.

**6** John and his force drew up facing them for battle. Seeing that his men were afraid to cross the stream, John crossed first; when the men saw it, they crossed after him.

**7** He divided the force and placed the cavalry in the midst of the infantry, for the enemy's cavalry was very numerous.

**8** They sounded the trumpets, and Cendebaeus was routed; many of his men fell wounded, and the rest fled into the stronghold.

**9** At that time Judas the brother of John was wounded, but John continued the pursuit until he came to Kidron, which Cendebaeus had built.

**10** Some of the enemy fled into the towers in the fields of Azotus, and John burned it with fire; about two thousand of them fell. He returned to Judea in peace.

**11** Now Ptolemy son of Abubus had been appointed commander over the plain of Jericho, and he had accumulated much silver and gold,

**12** for he was the son-in-law of the high priest.

**13** His heart grew proud and he planned to make himself master of the country; he devised treachery against Simon and his sons to destroy them.

**14** Simon was making a tour of the cities of the country and seeing to their welfare when he went down to Jericho — he and his sons Mattathias and Judas — in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month, that is, the month of Shebat.

**15** The son of Abubus received them with treachery into a small stronghold called Dok that he had built; he prepared a great banquet for them and had men hidden there.

**16** When Simon and his sons had drunk deeply, Ptolemy and his men rose up, took their weapons, rushed upon Simon in the banquet hall, and killed him along with his two sons and some of his servants.

**17** He committed a great act of treachery and repaid good with evil.

**18** Ptolemy wrote an account of all this and sent it to the king, asking him to send troops to help him and to hand over to him the country and the cities.

**19** He dispatched other men to Gazara to kill John, and sent letters to the commanders of thousands, inviting them to come to him, promising them silver, gold, and gifts.

**20** He also sent others to seize Jerusalem and the hill of the temple.

**21** But someone ran ahead and told John at Gazara that his father and brothers had perished, and that Ptolemy had sent men to kill him also.

**22** When John heard this, he was greatly shaken; he seized the men who had come to kill him and put them to death, for he knew that they had come to take his life.

**23** As for the rest of the acts of John — his wars, his valiant deeds, the walls he built, and all his achievements —

**24** these are written in the annals of his high priesthood, from the time he became high priest after his father.
